scope.side_model: KOTOR embeds client and server objects in one game process. logical_side is engine ownership, process_role is not inferred from a kp/nwscript name, and caller thread/Lua state is separate.

classifications.no_engine_io: Pure Lua/C++ value or string operation; no game memory, VM, client, or server object is accessed.
classifications.shared_vm_process_local: Runs in the injected process/Lua VM or reads/writes an address supplied by the caller; no intrinsic client/server owner can be established from the callback.
classifications.server_side: Reaches server-owned game objects, server world state, server tick, or server-side engine routines.
classifications.client_side: Reaches client-owned object/render/UI state or client-only engine calls.
classifications.both_client_server: The callback crosses or uses both embedded client and server state, or its observable effect is a server-to-client path.
classifications.unresolved_per_native: The bridge implementation is generic. Side depends on the selected native NWScript routine and its engine implementation; source does not justify a blanket server/client label.

uncertainties.detail: The bridge captures the specific CVirtualMachineInternal/CSWVirtualMachineCommands binding reached by the vm.run_script hook, then dispatches through that VM target. Static source does not establish that target as a multiplayer client or server process role; caller thread and Lua state are separate from engine logical side. A routine such as GetPosition or SendMessageToPC can be server-owned, client-visible, or cross-side; classify individual routines only after tracing its native implementation/profile. This artifact intentionally labels the generic entry unresolved_per_native rather than blanket server.

kp.struct.view is unresolved in this worktree because no set_address_resolver call was found. kp.struct.at and all direct View/Seq callbacks remain process-local side-agnostic even when a script happens to pass an engine address.

kp.console writes the process-local devtools console/output buffer when bound (the overlay may later render it in the client) and otherwise uses platform logging; classify the callback shared_vm_process_local. kp.feedback's logical effect is intended cross-side/client-visible feedback, but its exact native side remains unresolved_per_native because only generic VM calls are implemented here.

The service/configure/status records are process-local state, while native interception resolves both server PC identity and client creature/model resources. The Lua-facing operations are labeled both_client_server where they arm/toggle the hook.
